metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Powder River, WY
metaDescription: Own minerals near Powder River, WY, at the southern edge of the basin's oil trend? Get an offer grounded in the actual unit and formation.
heroLead: Powder River, Wyoming sits near the southern tip of the Powder River Basin in Natrona County, close enough to feel the pull of the horizontal drilling pushing down from Converse County.
intro: This little community shares its name with the basin it sits at the edge of, which can confuse people looking it up — but the geology is real. Natrona County's southern Powder River Basin acreage has seen renewed interest as operators extend Niobrara and Turner Sand horizontal units south out of Converse County, so mineral interests here can carry more upside than an old legacy stripper tract further from the trend.

Because this southern edge of the basin has been developed later than the core Converse County acreage, production and lease records here tend to be more recent, which we factor in alongside the state's activity data when tracing your interest.

sections.heading: Southern extension of the active drilling trend
paragraphs: Operators working the Powder River Basin have steadily extended horizontal units south toward this part of Natrona County as completion technology improved economics on thinner or deeper target zones. If your tract is inside or adjacent to one of those newer units, your interest is priced differently than an old vertical-well legacy fraction — there is more upside, but also less production history to lean on.

sections.heading: Ranch-country split estate
paragraphs: A lot of the land in this part of Natrona County has stayed in ranching use for generations, and mineral rights were sometimes reserved separately when parcels were sold or leased for grazing. If you inherited a mineral interest here without the surface, that is a common pattern and one we confirm through the county clerk's deed records.

sections.heading: What we need to price it
paragraphs: The legal description or a division order is the starting point. If your acreage is inside an active or recently permitted unit, we also check filings with the Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission before putting a number together.

faqs.question: Is my acreage close enough to the active drilling to matter for pricing?
faqs.answer: We check that specifically — proximity to permitted or producing units in the southern Powder River trend is one of the first things we look at.

faqs.question: I have ranch land here but I'm not sure I own the minerals under it.
faqs.answer: That's common in this area. We check clerk of court deed records to confirm whether the minerals were reserved separately from the surface.

faqs.question: What if there's no well on my tract yet?
faqs.answer: We still evaluate undeveloped acreage, weighted on nearby permitting and drilling activity.

faqs.question: Why does this area have less production history than Converse County?
faqs.answer: Development has moved south into this part of Natrona County more recently than the core Converse County trend, so lease and production records here tend to be newer.
